T_{\mathcal{P}}^{(\delta,\varepsilon)}(\theta') = \arg\min_{\theta \\mathcal{P}} \sum_{=1}^{n} w_i \rho_\delta(\theta'_i - \theta_i) + \varepsilon \, \|\theta - c\|_w^2. chain order structure δ=0.5\delta = 0.5:  block partition found algorithm :

T_{\mathcal{P}}^{(\delta,\varepsilon)}(\theta') = \arg\min_{\theta \\mathcal{P}} \sum_{=1}^{n} w_i \rho_{\delta_i}(\theta'_i - \theta_i) + \varepsilon \, \|\theta - c\|_w^2. wi∼𝒰[1,10]w_i \sim \mathcal{U}[1,10] δ=0.5\delta = 0.5:

title: Sequential Block Merging Algorithm for General Isotone Optimization Under Quadratic Loss
text: Given optimization variable 𝐱∈ℝn\mathbf{x}\\mathbb{R}^n, isotonic regression chain isotonic constraints given 𝗆𝗂𝗇𝗂𝗆𝗂𝗓𝖾𝐱12∥𝐱−𝐲∥22𝗌𝗎𝖻𝗃𝖾𝖼𝗍𝗍𝗈x1≤x2≤⋯≤xn. \begin{array}{rl}  \underset{\mathbf{x}}{\mathsf{minimize}} & \frac{1}{2}\left\|\mathbf{x}-\mathbf{y}\right\|_2^2 \\ \mathsf{subject}\text{ }\mathsf{} & x_1\leq x_2\leq \cdots\leq x_n. \end{array}
code: y <- 1:100 /10 + rnorm(100, 0, 3) y_calibrated <- solve_isotone_chain(y)$x  plot(1:100,y,type="o",col="red") lines(1:100,y_calibrated,col="blue")

title: Sequential Block Merging Algorithm for General Isotone Optimization Under Quadratic Loss
text: Given optimization variable 𝐱∈ℝn\mathbf{x}\\mathbb{R}^n, isotonic regression binary isotonic constraints given 𝗆𝗂𝗇𝗂𝗆𝗂𝗓𝖾𝐱12∥𝐱−𝐲∥22𝗌𝗎𝖻𝗃𝖾𝖼𝗍𝗍𝗈xi≤x2i,=1,…,⌈n2⌉,xi≤x2i+1,=1,…,⌈n−12⌉. \begin{array}{rl}  \underset{\mathbf{x}}{\mathsf{minimize}} & \frac{1}{2}\left\|\mathbf{x}-\mathbf{y}\right\|_2^2 \\ \mathsf{subject}\text{ }\mathsf{} & x_i \leq x_{2i} ,=1,\dots,\left\lceil \frac{n}{2}\right\rceil,\\  & x_i\leq x_{2i+1},=1,\dots,\left\lceil \frac{n-1}{2}\right\rceil. \end{array}  can solve problem plot results via package igraph.
code: library(igraph) p <- 20 # build a tree graph tr <- make_tree(p, children = 2, mode = "out") y <- 1:20 /10 + rnorm(20, 0, 3) y_calibrated <- solve_isotone_binary_tree(y)$x  V(tr)$name <- as.character(round(y_calibrated,2)) plot(tr,  vertex.size = 4,          # Smaller nodes     vertex.label = V(tr)$name, # Set the labels     vertex.label.cex = 1,   # Slightly smaller font     vertex.label.dist = 1.4,  # Offset the labels     vertex.label.color = "black")

title: Sequential Block Merging Algorithm for General Isotone Optimization Under Quadratic Loss
text: Given optimization variable 𝐱∈ℝn\mathbf{x}\\mathbb{R}^n, isotonic regression binary isotonic constraints given 𝗆𝗂𝗇𝗂𝗆𝗂𝗓𝖾𝐱12∥𝐱−𝐲∥22𝗌𝗎𝖻𝗃𝖾𝖼𝗍𝗍𝗈xi+(j−1)×⌊n⌋≤xi+1+(j−1)×⌊n⌋,∀=1,…,⌊n⌋−1,j=1,…,⌊n⌋xi+(j−1)×⌊n⌋≤xi+j×⌊n⌋,∀=1,…,⌊n⌋,j=1,…,⌊n⌋−1,xi≤xi+1,∀=⌊n⌋2,…,n−1. \begin{array}{rl}  \underset{\mathbf{x}}{\mathsf{minimize}} & \frac{1}{2}\left\|\mathbf{x}-\mathbf{y}\right\|_2^2 \\ \mathsf{subject}\text{ }\mathsf{} & x_{+(j-1)\times\left\lfloor\sqrt{n}\right\rfloor} \leq x_{+1+(j-1)\times\left\lfloor\sqrt{n}\right\rfloor} ,\forall =1,\dots,\left\lfloor\sqrt{n}\right\rfloor -1,j=1,\dots,\left\lfloor\sqrt{n}\right\rfloor\\  & x_{+(j-1)\times\left\lfloor\sqrt{n}\right\rfloor} \leq x_{+j\times\left\lfloor\sqrt{n}\right\rfloor} ,\forall =1,\dots,\left\lfloor\sqrt{n}\right\rfloor ,j=1,\dots,\left\lfloor\sqrt{n}\right\rfloor-1,\\  & x_i\leq x_{+1},\forall =\left\lfloor\sqrt{n}\right\rfloor^2,\dots, n-1. \end{array} can solve problem plot results via package igraph.
code: library(igraph) p <- 25 sqrt_p <- 5 E_mat <- c() # build a 2d-grid graph for(i in 1:4)   for(j in 1:5)      E_mat <- cbind(E_mat, c(i+(j-1)*sqrt_p, i+1+(j-1)*sqrt_p))  for(i in 1:5)   for(j in 1:4)      E_mat <- cbind(E_mat, c(i+(j-1)*sqrt_p, i+j*sqrt_p))  E_mat <- t(E_mat)  y <- 1:p /10 + rnorm(p, 0, 3) y_calibrated <- solve_isotone_2d_grid(y)$x  grid_graph <- graph_from_edgelist(E_mat) V(grid_graph)$name <- as.character(round(y_calibrated,2)) plot(grid_graph,  vertex.size = 4,          # Smaller nodes     vertex.label = V(grid_graph)$name, # Set the labels     vertex.label.cex = 1,   # Slightly smaller font     vertex.label.dist = 1.4,  # Offset the labels     vertex.label.color = "black")

text: can also define constraints graph long directed acyclic. example generate random DAG. using function Ordered_DAG, solve following problem 𝗆𝗂𝗇𝗂𝗆𝗂𝗓𝖾𝐱12∥𝐱−𝐲∥22𝗌𝗎𝖻𝗃𝖾𝖼𝗍𝗍𝗈xi≤xj,∀(,j)∈ℰ. \begin{array}{rl}  \underset{\mathbf{x}}{\mathsf{minimize}} & \frac{1}{2}\left\|\mathbf{x}-\mathbf{y}\right\|_2^2 \\ \mathsf{subject}\text{ }\mathsf{} & x_i \leq x_{j},\forall (,j)\\mathcal E. \end{array}
code: set.seed(12) start_nodes <- rep(1:10,3) end_nodes <- start_nodes + round(runif(30, 1, 5))  E_mat <- cbind(start_nodes, end_nodes)  DAG_graph <- graph_from_edgelist(E_mat)   DAG_graph <- simplify(     DAG_graph,     remove.multiple = TRUE,     remove.loops = TRUE,     edge.attr.comb = igraph_opt("edge.attr.comb") )  E_mat <- as_edgelist(DAG_graph)  y <- 1:max(E_mat)/2 + rnorm(max(E_mat), 0, 3) y_calibrated <- solve_isotone_DAG(y, rep(1,max(E_mat)), E_mat)$x  V(DAG_graph)$name <- as.character(round(y_calibrated,2)) plot(DAG_graph,  vertex.size = 4,          # Smaller nodes     vertex.label = V(DAG_graph)$name, # Set the labels     vertex.label.cex = 1,   # Slightly smaller font     vertex.label.dist = 1.4,  # Offset the labels     vertex.label.color = "black")

title: Implementing Sequential Block Merging Algorithm for General Isotone Optimization
text: basic example shows solve general isotonic regression problem: Using package igraph, can better view ordered vector regarding isotonic constraints edges graph. Namely, xi≤xjx_i\leq x_j exists arrow node ii node jj Projection Quadratic Loss Projection Huber Loss w Hyperparameter .5 typical isotonic constraints, including chain, binary tree, 2d-grid isotonic constraints, can defined directed. Simply using solve_isotone_chain, solve_isotone_binary_tree, solve_isotone_2d_grid, can solve corresponding isotone optimization problem!
code: library(IsotoneOptimization) ## basic example code  Emat <- t(matrix( c(1,2,  1,3,  1,4,  2,5,  2,6,  3,7,  4,8,  5,8,  6,9,  6,10),2,10)) # quadatic x_ordered <- solve_isotone_DAG(rnorm(10), rep(1,10), Emat)$x # Huber x_ordered_huber <- solve_isotone_DAG(rnorm(10), rep(1,10), Emat, loss = "huber", delta = .5)$x library(igraph) #>  #> Attaching package: 'igraph' #> The following objects are masked from 'package:stats': #>  #>     decompose, spectrum #> The following object is masked from 'package:base': #>  #>     union grid_graph <- graph_from_edgelist(Emat) V(grid_graph)$name <- as.character(round(x_ordered,2)) plot(grid_graph,  vertex.size = 4,          # Smaller nodes     vertex.label = V(grid_graph)$name, # Set the labels     vertex.label.cex = 1,   # Slightly smaller font     vertex.label.dist = 1.4,  # Offset the labels     vertex.label.color = "black") library(igraph) grid_graph <- graph_from_edgelist(Emat) V(grid_graph)$name <- as.character(round(x_ordered_huber,2)) plot(grid_graph,  vertex.size = 4,          # Smaller nodes     vertex.label = V(grid_graph)$name, # Set the labels     vertex.label.cex = 1,   # Slightly smaller font     vertex.label.dist = 1.4,  # Offset the labels     vertex.label.color = "black")
